question: Which novel by Kazuo Ishiguro won the Booker Prize in 1989 and was later adapted into an Oscar-nominated film?

options.text: An Artist of the Floating World

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Remains of the Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Remains of the Day** is a celebrated novel by the British author **Kazuo Ishiguro**, published in **1989**.
 
• This novel won the prestigious **Booker Prize** in the same year of its publication, making it one of Ishiguro's most recognized works.
 
• The story revolves around **Stevens**, an English butler, and explores themes of duty, regret, and the passage of time, as he reflects on his life and service to his employer.
 
• The book was later adapted into a critically acclaimed **Oscar-nominated film** in 1993</
